title: How Trump’s $5K payout promise can become crypto’s next liquidity shock
summary: Bitcoin is holding above $80k as institutional demand stays strong. Could Trump’s $5k initiative fuel a 2021-style liquidity-driven rally?
content: Bitcoin is currently holding steady above $80,000, supported by strong institutional demand. Market analysts are discussing whether a potential policy initiative by Trump could trigger a significant liquidity-driven rally, drawing comparisons to the market conditions seen in 2021.
content_ta: வலிமையான நிறுவன முதலீட்டு தேவையால் Bitcoin தற்போது $80,000-க்கு மேல் உறுதியாக உள்ளது. Trump-ன் புதிய கொள்கை திட்டம் மூலம் சந்தையில் பெரிய அளவில் பணப்புழக்கம் அதிகரித்து, 2021-ம் ஆண்டைப் போன்ற ஒரு விலை உயர்வு ஏற்படுமா என்பது குறித்து சந்தை ஆய்வாளர்கள் விவாதித்து வருகின்றனர்.

title: ANZ completes cross-border tokenised deposit payment with Swift ledger
summary: Australia's ANZ has carried out a live corporate treasury transactions using tokenised deposits and Swift’s blockchain ledger.
content: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group has successfully completed a live cross-border corporate treasury transaction using tokenised deposits. The financial institution utilized Swift's blockchain ledger to execute the payment, marking a significant step in exploring the practical applications of digital assets and distributed ledger technology for international banking and corporate financial operations.
content_ta: ஆஸ்திரேலியாவின் ANZ நிறுவனம், tokenised deposit-களைப் பயன்படுத்தி நேரலை cross-border கார்ப்பரேட் நிதிப் பரிவர்த்தனையை வெற்றிகரமாக முடித்துள்ளது. Swift-ன் blockchain ledger-ஐப் பயன்படுத்தி இந்தப் பணம் செலுத்தப்பட்டுள்ளது. சர்வதேச வங்கி மற்றும் கார்ப்பரேட் நிதி நடவடிக்கைகளுக்காக டிஜிட்டல் சொத்துக்கள் மற்றும் distributed ledger தொழில்நுட்பத்தின் நடைமுறைப் பயன்பாடுகளை ஆராய்வதில் இது ஒரு முக்கியமான படியாகும்.

title: U.S. scraps proposed $10,000 reporting rule for for crypto sent to private wallets
summary: FinCEN withdrew two proposals that had hung over self-custody and crypto mixers for years without ever taking effect.
content: The United States has scrapped a proposed reporting rule that would have required tracking of $10,000 for cryptocurrency sent to private wallets. FinCEN formally withdrew two proposals that had hung over self-custody and crypto mixers for years without ever taking effect, bringing relief to digital asset users and privacy advocates concerned about increased government oversight.
content_ta: பிரைவேட் வாலெட்களுக்கு அனுப்பப்படும் crypto பரிவர்த்தனைகளுக்கான 10,000 டாலர் reporting rule முன்மொழிவை United States கைவிட்டுள்ளது. எந்தவொரு அமலாக்கத்திற்கும் வராமல் பல ஆண்டுகளாக சுய-பாதுகாப்பு மற்றும் crypto mixers மீது தொங்கிக்கொண்டிருந்த இரண்டு முன்மொழிவுகளை FinCEN அதிகாரப்பூர்வமாக வாபஸ் பெற்றது.

title: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam test gets last-minute fix before major capacity jump
summary: One of Ethereum’s main validator clients updated its software hours before a Sepolia test that will raise the amount of work each block can hold to 200 million gas.
content: A major Ethereum validator client released an urgent software update just hours before a scheduled Sepolia testnet upgrade. The upcoming test aims to significantly increase network capacity by raising the block gas limit to 200 million. This crucial adjustment ensures validator stability ahead of the capacity jump, highlighting the network's ongoing scaling efforts.
content_ta: Sepolia testnet மேம்படுத்தலுக்கு சில மணி நேரங்களுக்கு முன்பு, ஒரு முக்கிய Ethereum validator client அவசர மென்பொருள் அப்டேட்டை வெளியிட்டது. பிளாக் கேஸ் வரம்பை 200 மில்லியனாக உயர்த்துவதன் மூலம் நெட்வொர்க் திறனை கணிசமாக அதிகரிப்பதை இந்த வரவிருக்கும் சோதனை நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டுள்ளது.

title: Bitcoin keeps getting rejected at $87,000 as stocks hover near records
summary: BTC fell back to about $85,600 after sellers turned it away from $87,000 for the third time since Sept. 23, while Nasdaq closed at a record and Treasury yields kept climbing.
content: Bitcoin dropped to approximately $85,600 after facing rejection near the $87,000 level for the third time since September 23. This downward movement occurred while the Nasdaq closed at a record high and Treasury yields continued to climb.
content_ta: செப்டம்பர் 23 முதல் மூன்றாவது முறையாக $87,000 நிலையைத் தாண்ட முடியாமல் சரிவைச் சந்தித்த Bitcoin, தோராயமாக $85,600 வரை சரிந்தது. இதற்கிடையில், Nasdaq புதிய சாதனை அளவிலும், கருவூல வருவாய் தொடர்ந்து உயர்ந்து கொண்டும் இருந்தது.

title: Solana Foundation unveils a program to settle institutional trades in seconds. JPMorgan gave input
summary: Solana Foundation launched an open-source program that lets institutions settle trades in seconds, not days. JPMorgan provided key inputs.
content: The Solana Foundation has launched an innovative open-source program designed to enable institutional financial trades to settle in seconds rather than days. The initiative aims to streamline market operations significantly. Notably, banking giant JPMorgan provided key input during the development of this new settlement program, marking a notable collaboration between traditional finance and blockchain technology.
content_ta: Solana Foundation நிறுவனமானது, நிறுவனங்களின் வர்த்தகங்களை நாட்கள் கணக்கில் இல்லாமல் வினாடிகளில் தீர்வு செய்ய உதவும் புதிய திறந்த மூல (open-source) திட்டத்தை அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இந்த புதிய தீர்வுத் திட்டத்தை உருவாக்குவதில் JPMorgan வங்கி முக்கிய உள்ளீடுகளை வழங்கியுள்ளது.

title: OKX eyes emerging markets with yield-offering stablecoin savings and payments app
summary: OKX Money lets users hold, send and spend dollar-backed stablecoins, with qualifying USDG balances earning up to 10% APY.
content: Cryptocurrency exchange OKX is targeting emerging markets with the launch of a new savings and payments application called OKX Money. The app allows users to hold, send, and spend dollar-backed stablecoins, enabling them to earn competitive yields on qualifying USDG balances as the company expands its financial services globally.
content_ta: கிரிப்டோகரன்சி எக்ஸ்சேஞ்ச் ஆன OKX, வளர்ந்து வரும் சந்தைகளை இலக்காகக் கொண்டு OKX Money என்ற புதிய சேமிப்பு மற்றும் கட்டண செயலியை அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இந்த செயலியின் மூலம் பயனர்கள் டாலர் ஆதரவு பெற்ற stablecoin-களை வைத்திருக்கவும், அனுப்பவும், செலவிடவும் முடியும். மேலும், தகுதியான USDG இருப்புகளுக்குக் குறிப்பிட்ட லாபத்தைப் பெறவும் இது வழிவகுக்கிறது.

title: Bitcoin futures drop $1.4B, but spot buyers step in to help
summary:
Glassnode’s weekly snapshot pairs a smaller derivatives footprint with rising holder activity, while spot buying supplies a counterweight.
The post Bitcoin futures drop $1.4B, but spot buyers step in to help appeared first on CryptoSlate.
content: Bitcoin futures experienced a significant drop of 1.4 billion dollars, reflecting a smaller derivatives footprint. However, spot buyers stepped into the market to provide a necessary counterweight, supported by rising overall holder activity as highlighted in recent data.
content_ta: Bitcoin futures-ൽ 1.4 பில்லியன் டாலர் சரிவு ஏற்பட்டுள்ளது, இது டெரிவேட்டிவ்களின் பங்கைக் குறைக்கிறது. இருப்பினும், நிலையான வாங்குபவர்கள் சந்தையில் நுழைந்து அதற்கு ஆதரவளித்துள்ளனர், மேலும் ஹோல்டர்களின் நடவடிக்கைகளும் அதிகரித்து வருவதாக தரவுகள் காட்டுகின்றன.

title: Kraken’s parent Payward taps Singapore Gulf Bank’s network for 24/7 settlements
summary: Payward is widening its institutional banking infrastructure as demand grows for faster, always-on movement between fiat and digital assets.
content: Kraken's parent company, Payward, has integrated Singapore Gulf Bank's network to enable round-the-clock settlements. This move expands Payward's institutional banking infrastructure as the demand increases for faster, always-on transactions between fiat and digital assets.
content_ta: Kraken நிறுவனத்தின் தாய் நிறுவனமான Payward, 24 மணி நேரமும் செயல்படும் செட்டில்மென்ட்களுக்காக Singapore Gulf Bank-இன் நெட்வொர்க்கை இணைத்துள்ளது. ஃபியட் மற்றும் டிஜிட்டல் சொத்துக்களுக்கு இடையே விரைவான மற்றும் தடையற்ற பரிவர்த்தனைகளுக்கான தேவை அதிகரித்து வரும் நிலையில், இந்த நடவடிக்கை Payward-இன் நிறுவன வங்கி கட்டமைப்பை விரிவுபடுத்துகிறது.

content: Veteran trader Peter Brandt has identified a potential bullish path for XRP. According to the legendary market analyst, the cryptocurrency could potentially rally toward a target of $2.16. This projection has drawn significant attention from market observers and traders monitoring the digital asset's recent price movements.
content_ta: அனுபவம் வாய்ந்த வர்த்தகர் Peter Brandt, XRP-க்கான ஒரு சாத்தியமான காளை சந்தை இலக்கை அடையாளம் கண்டுள்ளார். இந்த புகழ்பெற்ற சந்தை ஆய்வாளரின் கூற்றுப்படி, இந்த கிரிப்டோகரன்சி $2.16 என்ற இலக்கை நோக்கி உயரக்கூடும். இந்த கணிப்பு, டிஜிட்டல் சொத்தின் சமீபத்திய விலை நகர்வுகளைக் கண்காணிக்கும் சந்தை பார்வையாளர்களின் கவனத்தை ஈர்த்துள்ளது.

title: Benjamin Cowen Says Yields Could Fall After Midterms With a Potential Boost for Bitcoin
summary:
Benjamin Cowen expects Treasury yields to peak before mid-November. Here is what it could mean for Bitcoin and risk assets.
The post Benjamin Cowen Says Yields Could Fall After Midterms With a Potential Boost for Bitcoin appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: Analyst Benjamin Cowen predicts that Treasury yields could decline following the midterms around mid-November. According to the report, a potential drop in yields might provide a significant boost for Bitcoin and other risk-on assets as market conditions shift.
content_ta: இடைத்தேர்தல்களுக்குப் பிறகு, நவம்பர் மாத நடுப்பகுதியில் Treasury yields குறையக்கூடும் என்று ஆய்வாளர் Benjamin Cowen கணித்துள்ளார். இந்தச் சூழலில், yields-ல் ஏற்படும் சாத்தியமான சரிவு Bitcoin மற்றும் பிற risk-on assets-க்கு ஒரு பெரிய ஊக்கமாக அமையக்கூடும் என்று தெரிவிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: South Korea's AI Mania Spills Into Crypto, With Worldcoin as Top Pick
summary:
South Korean retail traders have carried their AI trade into crypto, Chainalysis data show. AI tokens became the top theme in won trading by June, with Worldcoin (WLD) drawing $7.41 billion in trading volume over the year. The demand has helped South Korea’s crypto economy grow 12.3% to $449.1 billion, even as East Asia’s contracted
The post South Korea's AI Mania Spills Into Crypto, With Worldcoin as Top Pick appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: South Korean retail traders have driven an increase in crypto trading, focusing heavily on AI-related tokens. Data from Chainalysis shows that AI tokens became a top theme in won trading by June, with Worldcoin emerging as a primary choice and drawing billions in trading volume. This surge in demand contributed to the growth of South Korea's overall crypto economy during the year.
content_ta: தென் கொரிய சில்லறை வர்த்தகர்கள் கிரிப்டோ வர்த்தகத்தில் அதிக ஆர்வம் காட்டி வருகின்றனர், குறிப்பாக AI-தொடர்பான டோக்கன்களில் கவனம் செலுத்துகிறார்கள். ஜூன் மாதத்திற்குள் won வர்த்தகத்தில் AI டோக்கன்கள் முக்கிய இடத்தைப் பிடித்ததாக Chainalysis தரவுகள் காட்டுகின்றன. இதில் Worldcoin முக்கியத் தேர்வாக உருவெடுத்துள்ளதுடன், மிகப்பெரிய அளவில் வர்த்தகப் பங்கை ஈர்த்துள்ளது. இந்த தேவையானது தென் கொரியாவின் கிரிப்டோ பொருளாதாரத்தின் ஒட்டுமொத்த வளர்ச்சிக்கு பெரிதும் உதவியுள்ளது.

title: Better Markets says the CFTC is the wrong cop for retail crypto
summary:

content: Advocacy group Better Markets argues that the CFTC is unsuited to oversee retail cryptocurrency, warning that expanding its regulatory role could weaken investor protections. The organization emphasizes the urgent need for clear and effective regulatory mandates to safeguard consumers participating in digital asset markets.
content_ta: சில்லறை வர்த்தக கிரிப்டோகரன்சி சந்தைகளைக் கண்காணிக்க CFTC பொருத்தமான அமைப்பு அல்ல என்று Better Markets அமைப்பு வாதிடுகிறது. அதன் ஒழுங்குமுறை பங்கை விரிவுபடுத்துவது முதலீட்டாளர் பாதுகாப்பை பலவீனப்படுத்தலாம் என்றும், நுகர்வோரைப் பாதுகாக்க தெளிவான கட்டுப்பாடுகள் தேவை என்றும் அந்த அமைப்பு எச்சரித்துள்ளது.

title: Google Cloud to shut down Blockchain Node Engine and hand customers to Quicknode
summary:
Google Cloud's exit from blockchain nodes may reshape infrastructure dynamics, boosting Quicknode's market position and influencing future partnerships.
The post Google Cloud to shut down Blockchain Node Engine and hand customers to Quicknode appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: Google Cloud is shutting down its Blockchain Node Engine and transitioning its existing customers to Quicknode. This strategic exit from the blockchain node infrastructure sector is expected to shift market dynamics and strengthen Quicknode's competitive position within the industry.
content_ta: Google Cloud தனது Blockchain Node Engine சேவையை மூடுவதாகவும், தற்போதைய வாடிக்கையாளர்களை Quicknode நிறுவனத்திடம் ஒப்படைப்பதாகவும் அறிவித்துள்ளது. பிளாக்செயின் நோட் உள்கட்டமைப்புத் துறையிலிருந்து கூகுளின் இந்த வெளியேற்றம் சந்தை நிலவரங்களை மாற்றி அமைக்கும் என்றும், Quicknode-ன் சந்தை நிலையை மேலும் வலுப்படுத்தும் என்றும் எதிர்பார்க்கப்படுகிறது.

title: Polymarket unveils Protocol V2, with full switchover for new markets on Nov 2
summary:
Polymarket's Protocol V2 enhances flexibility and efficiency, potentially reshaping market dynamics and developer engagement in prediction markets.
The post Polymarket unveils Protocol V2, with full switchover for new markets on Nov 2 appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: Polymarket has announced the release of Protocol V2, bringing improved flexibility and efficiency to prediction markets. The platform will transition completely to the new protocol for all new markets starting November 2. This upgrade aims to enhance overall market dynamics and increase developer engagement within the ecosystem.
content_ta: Polymarket நிறுவனம் Protocol V2 வெளியீட்டை அறிவித்துள்ளது, இது கணிப்பு சந்தைகளில் (prediction markets) நெகிழ்வுத்தன்மையையும் செயல்திறனையும் மேம்படுத்துகிறது. நவம்பர் 2 முதல் அனைத்து புதிய சந்தைகளுக்கும் புதிய நெறிமுறைக்கு முழுமையான மாற்றம் செய்யப்படும். இந்த மேம்படுத்தல் ஒட்டுமொத்த சந்தை இயக்கவியலை மேம்படுத்துவதையும் உருவாக்குநர்களின் ஈடுதலை அதிகரிப்பதையும் நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டுள்ளது.

title: World Bank raises East Asia growth outlook to 4.5%, warns of AI risks
summary:
East Asia's growth hinges on AI exports, but over-reliance and uneven adoption pose risks, potentially impacting long-term economic stability.
The post World Bank raises East Asia growth outlook to 4.5%, warns of AI risks appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: The World Bank has raised its economic growth outlook for East Asia to 4.5%. However, the institution issued a warning regarding artificial intelligence, noting that while growth heavily relies on AI exports, over-reliance and uneven adoption present significant risks that could threaten long-term economic stability in the region.
content_ta: கிழக்காசியாவின் பொருளாதார வளர்ச்சி குறித்த கணிப்பை World Bank 4.5 சதவீதமாக உயர்த்தியுள்ளது. அதேசமயம், AI ஏற்றுமதிகளை அதிகம் சார்ந்திருப்பதும், சீரற்ற முறையில் அதனை பின்பற்றுவதும் எதிர்காலத்தில் நீண்டகால பொருளாதார ஸ்திரத்தன்மைக்கு சவாலாக அமையலாம் என எச்சரித்துள்ளது.

title: OpenAI, Google, Meta, Anthropic lack insurance against catastrophic AI risk
summary:
The lack of insurance for catastrophic AI risks could lead to significant financial exposure for AI firms and influence regulatory actions.
The post OpenAI, Google, Meta, Anthropic lack insurance against catastrophic AI risk appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: Major artificial intelligence companies including OpenAI, Google, Meta, and Anthropic reportedly lack insurance coverage against catastrophic AI risks. Analysts note this absence of financial protection could expose these leading firms to substantial financial liabilities and potentially shape future government regulatory actions concerning the rapidly advancing technology sector.
content_ta: OpenAI, Google, Meta மற்றும் Anthropic போன்ற முன்னணி ஆர்டிபிஷியல் இன்டெல்லிஜென்ஸ் நிறுவனங்களிடம் பேரழிவு தரக்கூடிய AI அபாயங்களுக்கு எதிரான காப்பீடு இல்லை என்று கூறப்படுகிறது. இந்த நிதிப் பாதுகாப்பு இல்லாதது இந்த நிறுவனங்களுக்கு பெரிய அளவில் நிதிச் சுமையை உருவாக்கலாம் மற்றும் எதிர்கால ஒழுங்குமுறை நடவடிக்கைகளை பாதிக்கலாம் என்று கூறப்படுகிறது.

title: SpaceX Stock Rises as Morgan Stanley Backs $300 Target

summary:

content: The Bank of England's Digital Pound Lab has selected a consortium consisting of NOBO, D&B, and Polygon Labs. The group advances to Phase 2 to test stablecoin and digital pound settlement solutions focusing on SME cross-border trade finance.
content_ta: இங்கிலாந்து வங்கியின் டிஜிட்டல் பவுண்ட் லேப், NOBO, D&B மற்றும் Polygon Labs ஆகிய நிறுவனங்களைக் கொண்ட கூட்டமைப்பைத் தேர்ந்தெடுத்துள்ளது. சிறு மற்றும் நடுத்தர வணிகங்களின் எல்லை தாண்டிய வர்த்தக நிதியுதவிக்காக ஸ்டேபிள்காயின் மற்றும் டிஜிட்டல் பவுண்ட் தீர்வு முறைகளைச் சோதிக்க இந்தக் குழு இரண்டாம் கட்டத்திற்கு முன்னேறுகிறது.

title: Clea’s Sheriff Adedokun on Stablecoin Rails for African Importers
summary:
Clea founder Sheriff Adedokun explains how Nigerian importers pay overseas suppliers in fiat while stablecoins handle the settlement behind the scenes.
The post Clea’s Sheriff Adedokun on Stablecoin Rails for African Importers appeared first on The Fintech Times.
content: Sheriff Adedokun, founder of Clea, recently discussed how African importers handle international payments. According to Adedokun, Nigerian importers continue to pay overseas suppliers using traditional fiat currency. Meanwhile, stablecoins operate quietly in the background to handle the underlying settlement process efficiently, bridging the gap between traditional banking methods and modern digital assets for cross-border trade.
content_ta: Clea நிறுவனத்தை நிறுவிய Sheriff Adedokun, ஆப்பிரிக்க இறக்குமதியாளர்கள் எவ்வாறு சர்வதேச கட்டணங்களை மேற்கொள்கிறார்கள் என்பது குறித்து விளக்கினார். நைஜீரிய இறக்குமதியாளர்கள் பாரம்பரிய fiat நாணயங்களைப் பயன்படுத்தி வெளிநாட்டு சப்ளையர்களுக்கு பணம் செலுத்துவதாகவும், பின்னணியில் stablecoins மூலம் பரிவர்த்தனை தீர்வுகள் திறம்பட கையாளப்படுவதாகவும் அவர் தெரிவித்தார்.

title: Why bitcoin is down 'just' 32% a year after its record high of $126,000
summary: This shallower decline isn’t limited to the one-year anniversary. The bear market itself has been milder with past downturns seeing prices plummet 77% to 85%.
content: Bitcoin is currently trading down about 32 percent one year after reaching a record high of $126,000. Analysts note that this decline is relatively shallow compared to previous bear markets, which historically saw prices plummet between 77 percent and 85 percent, indicating a milder overall downturn for the cryptocurrency.
content_ta: Bitcoin தனது $126,000 சாதனை உச்சத்தைத் தொட்டு ஒரு வருடத்திற்குப் பிறகு தற்போது சுமார் 32 சதவீதம் குறைந்துள்ளது. கடந்த கால கரடி சந்தைகளில் விலைகள் 77 சதவீதம் முதல் 85 சதவீதம் வரை சரிந்ததை ஒப்பிடும்போது, இந்த வீழ்ச்சி ஒப்பீட்டளவில் குறைவாகவே உள்ளது என்று ஆய்வாளர்கள் குறிப்பிடுகின்றனர்.

title: EEZ tests atomic L1-to-L2 transaction in push to unify Ethereum
summary: An EEZ contributor shared a 0.001 ETH cross-chain test as the project develops a framework to connect Ethereum mainnet and its rollups.
content: An EEZ contributor successfully tested an atomic L1-to-L2 transaction using 0.001 ETH. This development is part of the project's broader push to build a framework that connects the Ethereum mainnet with its various layer-2 rollups, aiming to improve interoperability and unify the wider Ethereum ecosystem.
content_ta: Ethereum-ஐ ஒருங்கிணைக்கும் முயற்சியில், EEZ திட்டத்தின் பங்களிப்பாளர் ஒருவர் 0.001 ETH மதிப்பிலான atomic L1-to-L2 பரிவர்த்தனையை வெற்றிகரமாகச் சோதித்துள்ளார். Ethereum mainnet மற்றும் அதன் rollups-களை இணைக்கும் ஒரு கட்டமைப்பை உருவாக்கும் முயற்சியின் ஒரு பகுதியாக இந்தச் சோதனை நடத்தப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: China’s crypto ban Is failing to stop a $176 billion P2P economy
summary:
The July 2025–June 2026 data show rapid stablecoin reuse, while the share funding purchases remains unmeasured.
The post China’s crypto ban Is failing to stop a $176 billion P2P economy appeared first on CryptoSlate.
content: Despite China's strict cryptocurrency ban, data covering the period from July 2025 to June 2026 reveals a massive $176 billion peer-to-peer economy. The findings highlight rapid stablecoin reuse within the region, demonstrating that restrictions have failed to fully halt digital asset activity among users, though the exact share of funds used for direct purchases remains unmeasured.
content_ta: சீனாவின் கடுமையான cryptocurrency தடையை மீறி, July 2025 முதல் June 2026 வரையிலான தரவுகள் 176 பில்லியன் டாலர் மதிப்பிலான P2P பொருளாதாரத்தைக் காட்டுகின்றன. இப்பகுதியில் stablecoin பயன்பாடு வேகமாக அதிகரித்து வருவதை இந்த ஆய்வுகள் வெளிப்படுத்துகின்றன. தடை செய்யப்பட்ட போதிலும், டிஜிட்டல் சொத்து பரிவர்த்தனைகளை முழுமையாகத் தடுத்து நிறுத்த முடியவில்லை என்பதை இது காட்டுகிறது.

title: Cheap crypto capital hits wall as Bitfinex fee rule binds

content: Cheap cryptocurrency borrowing costs are facing new hurdles as updated fee rules from Bitfinex take effect. A published minimum fee means a sample one-year bond requires a notable upfront percentage, which calls into question the actual savings for borrowers seeking low-cost capital in the digital asset market.
content_ta: Bitfinex நிறுவனத்தின் புதிய கட்டண விதிகள் நடைமுறைக்கு வந்துள்ளதால், கிரிப்டோகரன்சி கடன் வாங்கும் செலவுகள் புதிய தடைகளை எதிர்கொண்டுள்ளன. வெளியிடப்பட்ட குறைந்தபட்ச கட்டணத்தின் காரணமாக, ஒரு வருட பாண்ட் மாதிரிக்கு கணிசமான முன்கூட்டிய கட்டணம் தேவைப்படுகிறது, இது டிஜிட்டல் சொத்து சந்தையில் குறைந்த செலவில்资本 நாடும் கடன் வாங்குபவர்களுக்கு உண்மையான சேமிப்பு கிடைக்கிறதா என்ற சந்தேகத்தை எழுப்புகிறது.

title: Solana News: DvP Targets Atomic Settlement
summary:

Morgan, the tool also aims to reduce the risk of one side paying without …

title: TOKEN2049 Singapore Schedule Puts Institutional DeFi on the 2026 Agenda
summary:
TOKEN2049 Singapore’s 2026 agenda pairs institutional finance with DeFi, on-chain trading and market structure—without confirming deals or launches.

title: Confide Unveils Agentic Governance Platform to Replace Fragmented GRC Point Solutions
summary:
Confide has unveiled its holistic agentic governance platform, bringing governance, risk and compliance (GRC) into one simple but powerful system and ending businesses' reliance on a patchwork of disconnected point solutions. The platform gives professionals a shared environment in which to set the standard for how GRC should run and put it into practice with AI agents, all whilst retaining full human oversight. Crucially, it is designed to govern not only people, but also the AI agents that increasingly work alongside them.
Confide was founded by Pav Gill, one of the most prolific whistleblowers in the history of financial services. It was built from his lived experience of the Wirecard scandal and his prior career as a general counsel working with legacy GRC software. Confide has been actively setting the standard for improved corporate governance since 2024, and this latest product iteration develops its capabilities further.
Pav Gill, Founder and CEO of Confide, said: “Businesses have spent years paying extortionate amounts for software that still leaves their people piecing together the events of internal incidents. When a serious concern arises, nobody should have to search across multiple systems to work out the individuals involved and how they handled the situation. Legacy GRC tools were never built for a world where billions of AI agents will help run companies, with humans in the loop. We built Confide to allow  professionals to defensibly manage and audit trail critical issues from start to finish, whether those issues involve people, AI agents or both.”
Regulatory pressure is only increasing. Around 61,000 new regulations are introduced each year, and companies are increasingly expected to prove compliance continuously rather than through periodic reviews. Buying a separate point solution for every new regulation is no longer viable, and regulators are holding more companies to account and demanding answers on how cases were managed, making defensibility essential. Organisations need to show who made each decision and the information driving these decisions.
Lax corporate governance and fragmented data have long been issues within scaling enterprises and large corporations, with news reports of whistleblowing allegations, HR cases and occupational fraud on the rise. In August, KPMG made headlines over its handling of a whistleblower who alleged that confidential client information had been improperly shared within the firm's Australian audit division to help win audit contracts from rival companies. Cases like this show the value of a single, defensible record that enables earlier detection and a clear account of how concerns were handled.
Confide brings case management, policy, risk and audit into one platform, with workflows for third-party risk, incident response, health and safety, law enforcement requests and AI governance. Policies, risks, cases, people, vendors and decisions connect in a single live governance record. When an issue arises, teams can see what happened, who or what was involved, what informed each decision and what action followed, without reconstructing the story across systems. The same model governs AI agents: businesses set which tasks agents can perform, where human approval is required and when people can step in. Agents handle routine administrative work while humans keep control of consequential decisions. Every action, by a person or an agent, is recorded in a defensible audit trail.
The platform is model-agnostic, with AI integrations designed to work with different models and existing ways of working. Teams can adopt its capabilities within the processes they already use, instead of overhauling their SOPs to adapt to a new tool.
Confide serves businesses across industries, with end users in over 150 countries. Its credentials include ISO 27001 certification and SOC 2 attestations. The company is backed by more than 50 global GRC leaders, including managing partners at international law firms, Internal Audit Beacon Award recipients, chief compliance officers of Fortune 100, and ISACA board members.  With this launch, Confide intends to set the standard for how organisations manage critical GRC workflows in the agentic-heavy years ahead.

title: Castles Technology Expands SoftPOS Flexibility with PCI MPoC Validation
summary:
Castles Technology, leader in Android payment acceptance solutions, has completed PCI Mobile Payments on COTS (MPoC) validation across all three elements of its SoftPOS portfolio, with its Attestation and Monitoring (A&M) Service and end-to-end MPoC Solution joining its previously validated MPoC Software.
The validation gives acquirers, payment service providers (PSPs), gateways and independent software vendors (ISVs) greater flexibility in how they bring SoftPOS services to market, whether integrating payment acceptance into an existing application, using Castles Technology to provide the security monitoring infrastructure behind it, or deploying a complete solution.
SoftPOS is becoming an increasingly established part of the payment acceptance landscape as businesses look for more flexible ways to take card payments across different environments. Phone-based acceptance can support use cases including table service, queue-busting, deliveries, field sales and pop-up retail, while also giving smaller businesses an alternative route into card acceptance without the need for a traditional payment terminal.
PCI MPoC provides a security framework for software-based payment acceptance on commercial off-the-shelf devices such as smartphones and tablets. Alongside payment acceptance itself, the standard places emphasis on the ongoing security of the device environment, including attestation and monitoring.
Castles Technology's portfolio has been designed to support partners at different stages of SoftPOS deployment. Its isolated MPoC SDK can be integrated into existing merchant or business applications, allowing partners to retain control over their branding, user experience and workflows. Its A&M Service, hosted and operated by Castles Technology, provides the supporting device attestation, security monitoring and risk assessment infrastructure, reducing the need for partners to build and operate that capability themselves. For organisations seeking a complete deployment model, its validated end-to-end MPoC Solution reduces development and integration requirements and can help accelerate commercial rollout. The CastlesPay MPoC Solution supports Android devices, with contactless acceptance and PIN entry on the device itself.
The portfolio sits alongside Castles Technology's Android payment terminals and CaSERV managed payment services, reflecting the company's view that phone-based acceptance extends, rather than replaces, dedicated payment hardware. Many businesses will operate across both environments, creating a need for consistent security, reliability and support across different points of acceptance.
Jean-Philippe Niedergang, CEO EMEA, Pacific and LATAM at Castles Technology, said: "SoftPOS has reached the point where the question for many payment providers is no longer simply whether to offer it, but how. Some want to own the entire experience, while others want to get to market quickly or avoid building complex security infrastructure themselves. By validating our software, our monitoring service and a complete solution, we can meet partners wherever they are in that journey and help them bring secure SoftPOS acceptance to market in the way that best fits their business."

title: Gatehouse Bank Launches Community Saver Account to Combat Youth Homelessness
summary:
Gatehouse Bank has today launched a one-year fixed term Community Saver Account in support of the Bank’s charity partner, Depaul UK, a youth homelessness charity. The account has been launched ahead of World Homeless Day this Saturday, and follows data indicating that, between 2024 and 2025, one young person aged 16-24 in the UK became homeless or at risk of homelessness approximately every four minutes.**
Through Gatehouse Bank’s Community Saver Account, customers can support Depaul UK simply by saving. Customers accept a profit rate that is 0.05% lower than the Bank’s standard Fixed Term Deposit rate and the Bank matches this contribution, resulting in a donation equivalent to 0.10% of the account deposit. All charitable contributions are transparent, measurable and administered directly by Gatehouse Bank.
Gatehouse Bank has partnered with Depaul UK since January 2025, with colleagues taking part in fundraising initiatives and hands-on volunteering, having already raised over £25,000 for the charity. Following a successful one-year partnership, it was announced that this had been extended until December 2027. The Community Saver Account will now allow the Bank’s customers to get involved and share their support, with funds raised directly helping Depaul UK to support young people through emergency accommodation, longer-term supported housing solutions and prevention programmes that stop homelessness before it starts.
Today’s launch comes five years after Gatehouse Bank introduced its range of Woodland Saver Accounts where, for every fixed-term deposit or cash ISA account opened or renewed, a tree is planted on the customer’s behalf in a UK woodland project certified by the government’s Woodland Carbon Code. As over a third (35%) of UK consumers would be willing to learn more about ethical savings products, there remains a strong appetite amongst savers to align their financial goals with their ethical values. The launch of the Community Saver Account provides customers with the opportunity to choose which ESG initiative they support, whether they prefer to focus on an environmental or social impact cause.
The Community Saver Account offers an expected profit rate (EPR)* of 4.15% and is available to all new and existing customers based in the UK, with a minimum deposit of £1,000.
Andy Homer, Chief Customer Officer at Gatehouse Bank, commented: “It has been fantastic to see the incredible work undertaken by Depaul UK to support young people across the UK and the impact it has on their lives. Recently, this involved providing 5,871 safe nights’ accommodation through its Nightstop network and reaching 11,152 people though its accommodation services, family support programmes and work in schools****.
“As an ethically conscious bank, we know this is a cause that many of our customers will also resonate strongly with. The Community Saver Account will allow customers to contribute in a meaningful way while still supporting them to achieve their personal savings goals.”
Alexia Murphy, CEO of Depaul UK, said: “It’s been great to see so many colleagues at Gatehouse Bank supporting our mission through fundraising and volunteering over the last two years and we are very excited to be announcing this next phase of our partnership ahead of World Homeless Day this weekend.
“The money raised really will make a difference to the young people we support. It costs just £53 to host a young person in crisis with Nightstop, our emergency accommodation. Trained and vetted Nightstop hosts provide a safe place to sleep, a hot meal, toiletries and a warm welcome to someone who has nowhere else to turn. We are so grateful to everyone who chooses to open an account and support Depaul UK.”

title: Hyundai Card and CEKAI Design 3D Motion Credit Card
summary:
Korean financial innovator Hyundai Card has launched the NAVER Hyundai Card Edition3, featuring a paradigm-shifting card design engineered in collaboration with globally acclaimed New York-Tokyo creator collective CEKAI.
The new card series departs from traditional static, flat card aesthetics by introducing 3D motion graphics to the physical plate, inspired by CEKAI’s 3D billboards for global brands like Nike, BMW, and Fendi.
Impressed by its playful, hyper-realistic images popping out of massive digital displays everywhere from New York’s Times Square to Tokyo’s Omotesando, Hyundai Card opted to work with CEKAI to bring dynamic 3D motion graphics to the hands of consumers. The collective had also established its reputation in Korea through its production of music videos for prominent artists like RM and Hyukoh.
From mid-2025, Hyundai Card and CEKAI began brainstorming ways to rethink the credit card medium. Drawing on its deep card design understanding, Hyundai Card took the lead in navigating material selection, packaging, and physical feasibility. Korean tech giant NAVER also provided an overarching design direction based on its brand assets. Within the foundational concept established by Hyundai Card and NAVER, CEKAI was given the creative freedom to come up with a paradigm-shifting card design.
Rather than first creating a flat 2D design and adding motion later, they designed the visuals and dynamic motion simultaneously. Having closely worked with Hyundai Card while going through over 100 draft designs to perfect the final product, they settled on a trio of striking plate options — two plastic and one metal.
Hyundai Card’s Design Lab then translated the designs into physical products. Using advanced laser techniques, they expressed the fine particles of the metal plate, while utilizing special films on the plastic plates to further accentuate the dynamic graphic elements. The resulting cards are: Plus, representing the limitless benefits of NAVER Plus Membership; Neo, channeling futuristic energy through color gradients and geometric graphics; and Logo Metal, where the NAVER logo appears to move thanks to motion graphic design cues.
"Currently, credit cards exist as physical plates, but we can easily imagine a future where they evolve into digital displays or take on entirely different forms,” said Kota Iguchi, CEKAI’s Creative Director and Motion Designer. “This project was incredibly exciting because of those diverse possibilities. I hope NAVER Hyundai Card members can feel that potential as well."
For Hyundai Card, too, design innovation remains a key aspect of its approach to new products. A Hyundai Card spokesperson commented, "This collaboration with CEKAI provided an excellent opportunity to expand the creative universe of Hyundai Card's design. We will continue our efforts to ensure the NAVER Hyundai Card is recognized not only for its premier financial benefits but also as a highly coveted item for its cutting-edge design."

title: Saxo Study on the Future of Digital Wealth Reveals Banks Increasingly Turning to External Partners Amidst AI Pressures
summary:
Banks are increasingly turning to external partners to modernise their wealth management and brokerage offerings, according to a new study about the future of digital wealth released by Saxo today.
The study, which surveyed 332 senior decision-makers across banking, brokerage, and fintech across Europe, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), and Asia-Pacific (APAC), points to an industry facing growing pressure to modernise.
Against this backdrop, financial institutions are reconsidering how they build and deliver their digital wealth capabilities, with half (50%) of respondents favouring a hybrid operating model that combines internal expertise with a single outsourced provider for the long term.
Digital wealth ambitions outpace execution
Despite growing pressure to modernise, majority of the financial institutions acknowledged they are still far from digital maturity in the study. Fewer than one-third (28%) of respondents described their wealth and brokerage capabilities as advanced. Most (43%) classified themselves as fairly advanced, with some ability to personalise client experiences and a partially digitised value chain.
The findings suggest that while digital transformation remains a strategic priority, many institutions continue to grapple with the complexity of upgrading technology, integrating systems and scaling digital capabilities across their organisations.
Legacy technology continues to hold banks back
Legacy technology remains a significant hurdle for these institutions. On average, respondents reported that their core wealth and brokerage technology stack is 6.7 years old, rising to 7.5 years among firms that manage these capabilities entirely in-house.
The findings also point to a gap between perception and reality. While three-quarters (75%) of respondents believe banks are well equipped to deliver digital wealth and brokerage propositions, nearly four in five (79%) say banks are launching new offerings without all the capabilities needed to support them.
The race to keep up with AI is intensifying
The research also uncovered growing concerns over the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on the competitive landscape. AI-driven robo-advisories and automated investment services emerged as the most-cited competitive threat (48%), ahead of Big Tech firms entering financial services (43%) and neo-brokers offering low- or zero-cost trading (36%).
Commenting on the research, Henrik Alsøe, Global Head of Institutional, Saxo Bank, said: “Banks are operating in an environment where both the opportunity and the pressure have never been greater. Growth in global wealth is creating significant business opportunity but advances in AI keep raising the bar. The challenge for many institutions is no longer recognising the need to modernise but modernising quickly enough to stay competitive. As a result, more are turning to strategic partners who can help them continually innovate, scale their offerings, and adapt to evolving client needs.”

title: Indemni Secures $4M Investment to Further Enhance Data-Led Insurance Technology
summary:
Indemni, the freight risk management and  insurance platform, today announced $4M of investment from Field Ventures and  Diagram Ventures in their latest funding round. 
Founded by Zach En’Wezoh, CEO, and Omar Draz, COO, Indemni was created to  address a critical weakness in freight security: the lack of reliable over-the-road data  and integrated processes for the freight and cargo industry. While existing carrier-vetting  platforms can confirm a company’s credentials during booking, the lack of system cohesion means it can fail at very basic verification processes such as confirming  whether the individual arriving at the facility is the assigned driver for the load.  
The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure, including microchips, server racks, and data  center hardware, means single trailer loads regularly reach values up to $15 million,  turning fraudulent pickups into catastrophic loss events. Indemni was built to bridge  this gap by aligning modern technology with underwriting. 
"Risk in transportation is constantly changing. Indemni has been a valuable resource as  we continue to strengthen our approach to protecting our customers’ shipments." – Tren Hopkins, VP of Risk Management & Compliance, Nolan Transportation Group 
Indemni closes this gap through a data-led proprietary rules engine that executes over  18 automated checks across the shipment journey. Before sensitive load information or  rate confirmations are released, the platform uses a unique set of parameters to verify  who is collecting the freight, confirm equipment details, check relevant documentation,  collect photographic evidence, and track shipments, all in real time. Every completed  check is stored in a central audit trail, giving customers immutable records for shipper  reviews and insurance claims. 
“We are setting the new standard for freight insurance by bringing over-the-road  intelligence data directly to the teams insuring HVHR loads. By rewarding verified  operational controls with better coverage and pricing, Indemni is building the world’s  first insurance platform using cloud-based technology to eliminate physical supply  chain risks.” – Zach En’Wezoh, CEO, Indemni 
With the insurance industry becoming increasingly reliant on dependable, wide-ranging and fast-moving data sets to accurately assess risks, Indemni allows the traditionally  analogue world of insurance to tap into burgeoning tech capabilities through its  propriety blend of systems. Data requests that would have previously taken hours to complete are now searchable and verifiable in real time, streamlining checks to  drastically increase efficiency as well as security.  
To this end, Indemni are proud to have secured the coveted status of a ‘Lloyd’s  Coverholder’ – providing the world’s largest insurance and reinsurance marketplace  with access to its product offering. Chaucer, a leading global specialty (re)insurance  group who is sponsoring Indemni’s insurance program, recognizes the advantage of  building a specialized underwriting engine with a technology-first approach. 
“Cargo theft is an established marine risk, but the methods being used are becoming  increasingly sophisticated and evolving beyond traditional physical theft; with criminals  increasingly using fraud, impersonation and manipulation of legitimate freight  processes to gain control of shipments. As those exposures evolve, the insurance  market needs to adapt with relevant solutions. Indemni brings a focused approach to a  growing challenge for cargo owners and the logistics sector, combining specialist  insurance protection with strong risk management. We are pleased to lead the  programme and support its launch into the market.” – Simon Schnorr, Head of Marine  & Energy, Chaucer

title: What stablecoin card adoption numbers actually measure

title: Wise Adds Flexible eSIM Data Plans and Cross-Border QR Payments
summary:
Ahead of the peak year-end travel season, Wise, the global technology company building the best way to move and manage the world's money, has launched a direct fix for "arrival anxiety" - the universal moment of panic of landing in an unfamiliar country without mobile data or the local way to pay. By combining customizable eSIM data plans with an unmatched cross-border QR code scanner that works across five continents, Wise becomes the first to combine the two in one app.
A new Wise-commissioned YouGov survey of more than 14,000 travelers across eleven countries, found that 62% of adults who have traveled internationally in the last year rely on hotel or accommodation Wi-Fi to stay connected abroad. Once outside their hotel, travelers resort to comical behaviors to stay connected:
24% of travelers have bought something at a café they did not want, purely to get free Wi-Fi.
15% have stood outside a museum or tourist attraction to use their free Wi-fi instead of going inside.
7% have asked a total stranger to share their phone's personal hotspot.
Cash management was the most common payment problem reported abroad (43%). Of those who experienced challenges almost 40% of travelers said they missed out on local experiences like street food markets. Wise is solving both these pain points: the eSIM keeps people connected, while the extensive QR code payments network helps travelers pay like a local.
Waste-free, Build-Your-Own eSIM plans


One-time eSIM installation: Customers only need to download the eSIM to their device once rather than for each individual trip.
Custom Controls: Travelers can buy the data directly from the Wise app, set the exact data allowance and the exact number of days they need, mapped perfectly to their itinerary.
Data Estimation Guidelines: Intuitive, in-app guidelines to help customers avoid over or under-buying data before they depart.
Unused Data Plan Refund: Wise will refund travelers for any unused data plans they purchase but do not use. Handy for those times when travel plans change.
Instant Activation: The data will only be used when the eSIM is connected to the supported network at the destination.
One app for the world's QR codes


Pay like a local from Singapore to Budapest to Rio de Janeiro: Wise's direct connections with local payment schemes such as PayNow (Singapore), QR Ph (Philippines), DuitNow (Malaysia), Pix (Brazil), PromptPay (Thailand), Swiss QR-bill (Switzerland) and Qvik (Hungary) means that for the first time, all of these local payment schemes are now available in one place - through the Wise app.
Unlocking cashless payment in the Chinese mainland and beyond*: Through a strategic partnership with the Alipay+, Ant International's unified wallet gateway network, Wise has simplified payments for travelers visiting Asia. In the Chinese mainland, where cash and foreign card payments are not commonly accepted, eligible Wise travelers can scan the QR and pay at millions of local Alipay+ enabled merchants directly through the Wise app without needing a Chinese bank card, local mobile number, or separate app setup required. The partnership enables Wise users to make cross-border QR payments in 50+ destinations globally including Hong Kong, Nepal, Korea, Sri Lanka and Cambodia.

title: Ecommpay Helps Merchants Reach More Vietnamese Customers
summary:
Helping e-commerce merchants expand across borders, inclusive global payments platform, Ecommpay, has added VietQR to the alternative payment methods (APMs) available to its merchant partners. Connecting more than 2 million businesses with 50 million registered users across Vietnam and 60+ participating banks, VietQR supports hundreds of millions of transactions each month.
With VietQR preferred by around 70% of shoppers in Vietnam, its addition to the Ecommpay platform means customers can pay using an app they already know and trust, and their preferred Vietnamese banking app or digital wallet, removing the need to enter card details or download a new app. Simplifying local payments, customers can pay directly from their bank account or supported Vietnamese e-wallet, and payment details are automatically displayed in Vietnamese Dong (VND) ready for the customer to review and approve securely.
“Customers will often abandon a purchase if they cannot pay with their preferred local payment method, so we are committed to offering as many payment methods as possible,” commented Max Ryzhov, Chief Product Officer, Ecommpay. “With VietQR now available for our merchant partners to add to their payment options, we are helping merchants reach more Vietnamese customers. VietQR provides our merchant partners with an easy way to expand into the Vietnamese market and its growing digital payments market, by offering local customers a smoother and more familiar checkout.”
While payments are presented to the customer in VND, they can be settled in EUR or USD, depending on the merchant’s preference, to simplify local payments and can typically be settled the next business day  The payment status is updated as soon as the transaction is confirmed, helping merchants process orders quickly.
VietQR through Ecommpay is available via desktop or mobile and compatible with banking apps and supported Vietnamese payment apps i.e. digital wallets to ensure a seamless payments experience for every customer. And the interoperable model means merchants can display one QR code while customers choose how they want to pay – whether through their bank or a supported digital wallet.

title: finmid Raises €17M and Expands into Vehicle Financing and Marketplace Loans for the First Time with Bolt and Skroutz
summary:
finmid, the Berlin-based embedded lending company behind the financing programmes of Wolt, Delivery Hero and myPOS, is today announcing it has raised €17m from Big Pi Ventures and Mainset, with Earlybird following on, as it launches two of its most significant products to date: multi-year vehicle financing with Bolt, and a merchant lending programme with Skroutz. 
The Series A extension brings finmid's total funding to €52m. The capital will be used to expand finmid's asset-finance products, multi-source funding infrastructure and underwriting capabilities, and to support expansion into further platform categories including mobility and e-commerce.
Bolt Vehicle Solutions
Ride-hailing platform Bolt has partnered with embedded lending infrastructure provider finmid to launch Bolt Vehicle Solutions, a programme that gives fleet operators access to tailored vehicle financing. 
Europe’s ride-hailing market is projected to reach €157 billion by 2034, yet the fleet operators serving this demand face a structural challenge when it comes to financing vehicles. Traditional lenders often lack visibility into the commercial performance of fleet businesses, and vehicle manufacturers’ standard financing terms are not designed for high-utilisation commercial use.
Bolt Vehicle Solutions addresses this gap directly. Operators can explore available vehicles on the platform and, when ready, are connected to finmid to review financing options and complete their application. finmid’s terms provide for fixed monthly repayments, with ownership transferring on final payment - turning what was a recurring cost into a long-term asset.
Skroutz Funding 
Through its partnership with Skroutz, Greece's largest online marketplace, finmid powers Skroutz Funding, enabling the marketplace to lend directly to its around 9,000 merchants, with Skroutz Group providing the capital and finmid handling the underwriting, regulated lending, servicing and refinancing. It is the first finmid partnership in which its credit infrastructure wraps around the platform's own source of capital.
Building on momentum
finmid was founded on the belief that business financing is moving into the platforms businesses already use and trust. It builds the lending infrastructure that makes this possible across Europe: through a single integration, platforms can offer their business customers financing, with finmid handling the underwriting, regulated lending and servicing, and capital coming from the platform itself, its banking partner or finmid’s refinancing partners.
Today’s news is finmid’s first funding announcement since its €23m Series A in April 2024. Since launch, finmid has extended more than €4bn in financing offers to businesses across 30 European markets, working with partners including Wolt, Delivery Hero, myPOS and efood. And businesses keep coming back: around 85% of borrowers return for further financing, while financed merchants have grown their revenue on partner platforms by as much as 45%. Both of today’s launches, as well as the latest funding, mark the next stage in that journey – having proved its model with working capital, finmid is now applying the same infrastructure to bigger and more complex financing problems faced by platforms and the businesses that rely on them.
Alexander Talkanitsa, co-founder, finmid said: "Two years ago, embedded lending meant a cash advance for a restaurant. Today the same rails carry a multi-year vehicle loan, a marketplace's own balance sheet, and the potential for more. Every platform with business customers now has a way to become their financing partner without becoming a bank."
Max Schertel, co-founder, finmid said: "Small businesses have never lacked ambition – they've lacked a lender who could see them. Platforms, with their live and embedded view of the businesses they power, are uniquely placed to fill that gap, and finmid exists to make it happen. With Bolt we're financing the cars that fleets run on; with Skroutz the marketplace itself is putting its capital behind its merchants. Our job is to make that credit safe, fast and regulated – whoever provides the money and whatever businesses need it for."
Joshua Okeleke, Europe BD Lead, Bolt said: "Fleet operators are essential to making ride-hailing work, but access to vehicles and financing can be a real barrier to growing their businesses. With Bolt Vehicle Solutions, we’re helping remove that barrier by combining preferential vehicle deals with a simpler path to financing and, ultimately, ownership. That gives our fleet partners a stronger foundation to invest in their businesses, put more vehicles on the road and grow alongside rising passenger demand.”
 

Nick Kalliagkopoulos, Partner, Big Pi Ventures said: “Embedded lending is now essential infrastructure for marketplaces, and finmid is built to deliver it. Their capital light structure lets them grow quickly, and their licensing and geographic foothold make them a partner marketplaces can plug in once and scale everywhere. Their traction in southeast Europe, a region many overlook despite its size, is proof of how much whitespace is still out there.”

title: Walker Crips Selects WealthAI for Firm-Wide AI Rollout
summary:
WealthAi, the AI operating system built specifically for wealth managers, EAMs, family offices and financial advisors, has been selected by Walker Crips, the £4.5bn assets under management and administration (AUMA) UK investment management firm, as its AI operating system across its business.
Walker Crips will initially deploy WealthAi's compliance agents to help its teams monitor, flag and audit client communications, significantly reducing reliance on manual spot-checks and spreadsheets. The agents integrate with existing systems and can analyse structured and unstructured data across email, voice and documents.
Walker Crips will then expand the rollout to 70 users across its business, bringing employees and AI agents together on a single platform where they can work with and share information across the business. WealthAi's operating system creates a 'closed loop' for Walker Crips personnel and operations meaning that they and the AI agents are collaborating and sharing information in a safe, secure and entirely private environment.
Sean Lam, CEO of Walker Crips, said: "What attracted us to WealthAi was that they’ve moved beyond single-purpose AI tools and built something specifically for wealth management, one that understands the regulatory complexity and need for trusted, explainable intelligence our sector demands.
“It’s not just about digitising old processes, but giving advisers and operations teams the ability to pull in vast amounts of information, question it intelligently, turn it into real insight and use that to make better decisions for our clients and our business.”
Jason Nabi, founder and CEO of WealthAi, commented: “The firms that succeed with AI won’t simply digitise existing processes; they’ll rethink how knowledge and expertise are delivered across the organisation and to clients. AI is moving fast and this is an exciting opportunity to show what enterprise AI can look like across a wealth management firm.”
Walker Crips joins a growing number of wealth management firms using WealthAi, and the partnership follows a series of new product launches from WealthAi this year, including AI agents for KYC and client onboarding, WealthAi for Advisors and its Compliance Solution.

title: More Brits Say High Street Banks Have Worsened as Digital Rivals Pull Ahead
summary:
Traditional high street banks and building societies are losing ground to digital challengers on service quality, according to new research.
The findings from CRIF – a global leader in credit and insurance information, analytics and solutions – show that traditional banks and building societies are the only type of financial provider where UK consumers are more likely to say service has worsened than improved over the past three years (29% vs 26%).
Three in ten (29%) consumers say service from traditional banks and building societies has worsened over the last three years, compared with just 7% who say the same of digital banks and fintechs. By contrast, digital providers are far more likely to be seen as improving, with 43% of consumers saying their service has improved.

Digital banks and fintechs are firmly in positive territory for service improvement, while traditional banks and building societies are the only provider type with a negative net score.
Sara Costantini, Regional Director for the UK & Ireland at CRIF, said: “Digital banks and fintechs are setting the standard for what good looks like in financial services, and consumers can see the difference.
“What is striking is how traditional banks are falling behind. It’s clear that consumers broadly welcome the rise of digital banking services but remain frustrated when this digitisation leaves them with poorer services that lack human support. As the only provider type that customers think has worsened rather than improved, incumbents can no longer rely on their scale or legacy alone to retain customers.”
Branch closures leave one in five without support
UK consumers have broadly welcomed the rise of digital financial services, with two in five (41%) saying they have made managing their money easier, while almost half (48%) say they are able to manage their finances 24/7.
But a significant minority feel the shift has come at a cost. One in five (20%) say bank branch closures have made it harder to get the support they need, while 16% say the growth of digital services has led to a decrease in service quality and 15% believe digital services have only been introduced to reduce providers’ costs.
Costantini added: “The banks that will win out are those that match the challengers on digital experience without leaving behind the people who relied on in-person services. The opportunity for high street banks is clear: combine trusted brands and longstanding customer relationships with smarter use of data, analytics and digital services. Those that can deliver both convenience and confidence will be best placed to win the next generation of customers.
“In the end, customers do not choose between digital and human banking. They expect both. The winners will be the institutions that use technology not just to make banking faster, but to make it feel more personal, relevant and reassuring.”
The findings come as separate research shows that nearly half of UK consumers (49%) have now opened a digital-only bank account, up from 40% in 2025 and 36% in 2024.*
The research forms part of CRIF’s 2026 Banking on Banks report series. The first report, launched in June, looks at the biggest financial pressures currently facing European consumers and businesses. The second report, due to be published later in October, will look at the financial services gap between consumers and businesses.

title: PayDo Selects Convera to Expand SWIFT Receivables and Onward Cross-Border Payments
summary:
The collaboration brings expanded SWIFT receive capabilities into PayDo’s existing platform, helping customers manage incoming and onward international payments through a more connected experience.
By bringing Convera’s global payment capabilities into PayDo’s existing platform, customers will be able to receive funds via SWIFT and manage onward payment flows through a more connected experience, without PayDo having to build the underlying capability independently.
Extending SWIFT Receive Capabilities Without Additional Banking Infrastructure
For payment providers, enabling clients to receive funds via SWIFT can require additional banking relationships and significant supporting infrastructure. Through its partnership with Convera, PayDo can extend this capability through its existing platform, reducing the need to build and manage that infrastructure independently.
The integration also strengthens the way payments move through PayDo's platform. Connecting PayDo’s client experience with Convera’s global payment network delivers fewer provider relationships, easier reconciliation, and a clearer receive-to-onward-payment workflow.
PayDo processes over €5 billion annually for more than a thousand businesses across e-commerce, digital goods, iGaming, and financial services. Its model is built on reducing the fragmentation that can force businesses to maintain separate relationships for acquiring, accounts, payouts, and currency conversion. Convera extends that approach to receiving and moving funds internationally, giving PayDo a way to add SWIFT receive capabilities through its existing platform.
“Our aim is to give businesses one simpler way to manage the different stages of their payment journey”, – said Serhii Zakharov, CEO and founder of PayDo. “Working with Convera enables us to extend how clients receive international funds through the PayDo platform and move them onward with less operational complexity”.
Convera combines global payment infrastructure with more than 40 years of foreign exchange and cross-border payments expertise, moving nearly $200 billion in payments annually. Its network supports more than 140 currencies across 200+ countries and territories. Bringing that scale and capability into PayDo’s platform will help create a more connected experience for businesses receiving and moving money internationally.
“Growing businesses need international payments to work as one connected flow, not as a series of separate accounts, providers and integrations”, – said Meaghan Riley, Chief Commercial Officer at Convera. “By combining PayDo’s client experience with Convera’s global payments network and expertise, we are making it simpler for businesses to receive and move money internationally as they grow”.
Building a More Connected International Payment Experience
Working with Convera, supports PayDo’s strategy of bringing complementary payment capabilities into one client experience. By extending that model to international payment receipt and onward processing, PayDo can serve a broader range of customer payment needs while maintaining a simpler, more connected experience.

title: The Cost of Managing Multiple Payment Providers: Where the Money Actually Goes
summary:
Often, payment teams I speak with can quote their blended processing rate to two decimal places. Very few can tell me what it costs to run the providers that rate covers. That second number is usually larger, and it grows faster than the first.
Multi-provider setups are now mainstream. In our State of Payment Maturity 2025 study, the share of businesses connected to five or more providers rose from 24.6% to 37.1% in a single year. Yet 58.5% of respondents still run what we classify as fragmented payments: several systems working in parallel. That gap is where the real cost of managing multiple payment providers sits — not in the fee schedule, but in the payment operations around it.
The six cost lines below are the ones I see most often across the payment companies, merchants, and platforms we work with. Each has a way to measure and reduce it without giving up the providers you need.
Six costs of managing multiple payment providers that never hit the invoice
In a multi-PSP setup, each new provider adds an API to maintain, a statement format to reconcile, a decline taxonomy to translate, and another variable in every routing decision. Because each provider touches every process you already run, these costs multiply with the provider count while fees only add up.
 

1. Integration upkeep
The build is the cheap part. Once a provider goes live, its maintenance clock starts: API version changes, deprecated fields, new 3D Secure flows, certificate rotations, and webhook formats that shift with little notice. None of it appears in the original estimate, because none of it happens during the build.
Our data shows how much of this burden teams still carry. While 43.9% of businesses can add a new provider or payment method within days, 27.8% describe every integration as a significant project or a months-long effort. If the cost of maintaining your direct connections almost cancels out the value of having them, that is the signal to watch.
2. Data assembly
Every provider reports in its own dialect: its own transaction IDs, timestamps, status models, and decline codes. Someone has to turn five exports into one answer to a simple question, such as why approval rate dropped on Tuesday.
That someone is usually your most expensive payment specialist. In our analysis of 112 job descriptions for The State of the Payment Manager Role 2026, reporting and analytics was the most frequently named responsibility, mentioned 69% more often than PSP management, and Excel was the most-mentioned tool.
3. Reconciliation and settlement drift
Each provider settles on its own schedule, in its own currencies, and net of its own fees and reserves. Matching it all back to orders and bank statements is where multi-provider finance teams lose days at month-end. Multi-currency flows add another layer: when providers convert at different rates and points in the flow, small discrepancies accumulate into variances finance has to explain.
Across the multi-provider setups we onboard, reconciliation is still most often done by hand, and it routinely takes specialists days each cycle. But the hours are only part of the bill. Unreconciled balances delay settlement visibility, slow down dispute handling, and leave treasury forecasting cash it cannot fully confirm.
4. Silent approval leaks
Providers rarely fail cleanly. More often, approvals sag on one BIN range, one currency, or one corridor while every dashboard looks normal. Without central monitoring, the drop surfaces in the weekly report, after the revenue is gone.
A simple illustration: a business processing 200,000 card transactions a month at a $60 average ticket routes 30% of its volume through one acquirer. That acquirer loses four approval points for ten days. Roughly 800 payments fail, about $48,000 in attempted sales. Even if half of those customers retry successfully, $24,000 disappears without a single alert firing.
We sometimes see this pattern: approvals in one currency turn unstable because a single provider carries that currency alone and starts going down. The problem stays hidden until someone reviews live performance data, and the fix is usually a second provider plus a cascading rule.
That delay matters because approval rate is the metric payment teams answer for: it is the most frequently named KPI in Payment Manager job descriptions, at 14.1% of all KPI mentions.
5. Change latency
The most expensive line is often the one nobody records: the time between deciding to do something and being able to do it. Launching a local payment method, adding an acquirer for a new market, or shifting traffic away from an underperforming provider all queue behind engineering when routing logic lives in code.
For a business expanding region by region, new providers are routine. When each connection still takes months to go live, every month of that delay is a month the market converts below its potential.
6. Unused negotiating power
Multiple providers should strengthen your position in every pricing conversation. In practice, many businesses cannot move volume fast enough for that option to be credible. If shifting 20% of traffic requires a sprint, your providers know it, and your next price review reflects it.
The same rigidity keeps weak providers in the stack. Without comparable approval, cost, and uptime data per provider, nobody can prove which one should lose volume, so legacy connections keep processing out of habit.
How to calculate what your provider portfolio really costs
Payment provider management becomes much easier to discuss with a CFO once you express it in money rather than SLAs. To get a first estimate, pull six figures for the last quarter, one for each cost line:
 

 


Engineering hours spent on provider changes, fixes, and upgrades, multiplied by your loaded hourly cost.
Analyst and payment-team hours spent building reports by hand from provider exports.
Days to close month-end reconciliation, plus the number of exceptions still open afterwards.
Time to detect an approval drop at a single provider, and the volume processed during that window.
Lead time to add a provider, acquirer, or payment method, from signed contract to first live transaction.
Share of your volume you could move to another provider within one day.
 
The first three give you direct operating cost. The fourth and fifth estimate revenue at risk. The last shows how much pricing power you actually hold. In my experience, teams that run this exercise for the first time are surprised by how close the operational total comes to the fee savings they negotiate so hard for.
Why cutting providers is the wrong fix
Faced with these numbers, the tempting conclusion is to consolidate back to one or two providers. For a business selling in one country at modest volume, that can be sensible: a single provider is still the most common setup among single-country businesses in our data, at 40.9%. For anyone crossing borders or scaling volume, it usually is not. Coverage, local acquiring, and approval performance genuinely require a multi-acquirer setup, which is why 43.5% of businesses processing over 500,000 transactions a month run 10+ providers.
 

What separates the businesses that make multi-PSP pay off is how they run their providers. Our maturity data shows the shift clearly: among businesses with one provider, 44.4% rely on basic payment acceptance alone. Among those with ten or more, that share falls to 7.4%. At five to nine providers, advanced features (31.6%), AI/ML automation (17.0%), and routing hubs (15.5%) start to appear in force. Mature teams build a control layer around their providers. Teams that skip it simply buy more of the six costs above.
How to cut the cost without cutting providers
Each of the six cost lines has a structural fix. None of them requires removing a provider you need.
Normalize before you optimize. Map every provider to one transaction model, one status model, and one decline taxonomy. Until declines speak one language, every investigation starts with translation.
Take routing and failover out of code. Define routing by BIN, geography, currency, payment method, and cost, with cascading to the next best provider on failure. A routing change should be a configuration update, not a release.
Unify reporting and reconciliation. One source of truth for performance across providers, with automated matching against each provider's statements, removes the data assembly and month-end drift in one move.
Give the portfolio an owner. Nearly 60% of companies still manage payments as an administrative task or a secondary responsibility, and the mid-market is the most exposed: 67.4% of businesses processing 500–5,000 transactions a month run payments this way. Dedicated ownership rises from 25% at the smallest volumes to 73.1% above 500,000 transactions, according to our research. Someone needs authority over routing and provider mix, not just responsibility for reporting on it.
Review providers like a portfolio. Score every provider quarterly on approval rate, cost, uptime, and reconciliation exceptions. Shift volume toward those that earn it and retire the rest.
The payment routing fix alone moves numbers further than most teams expect. In one collaboration, we rebuilt a client's routing to send each transaction to the provider with the best approval rate for its type, cascade on failure, and take the cheaper route when approval rates were level. Conversion went from 56.2% to 85.1% within a year. At Corefy, we run all five of these fixes in one orchestration layer with 650+ ready-made integrations, so adding a provider doesn't add a new process to manage.
Key takeaways
Managing multiple payment providers is the default for any business selling across borders or at scale, and that will not reverse.
PSP fees are the visible cost. Integration upkeep, data assembly, reconciliation drift, silent approval leaks, change latency, and unused negotiating power are the larger ones.
These costs multiply with every provider because each one touches every process you already run.
The fix is a single control layer and a clear owner, not fewer providers.
Multi-provider setups are here to stay, and for most growing businesses they should be. What decides whether they pay off is whether the providers run as one system, with shared data, central routing, and a clear owner, or as a collection of separate connections. content: Managing multiple payment providers involves hidden operational costs beyond basic fees, including integration upkeep, data assembly, reconciliation drift, silent approval leaks, change latency, and unused negotiating power. Rather than cutting providers, businesses can resolve these challenges by implementing a unified control layer, centralizing routing, automating reporting, and assigning dedicated portfolio ownership to streamline multi-provider payment operations efficiently.
content_ta: பல கட்டண வழங்குநர்களை நிர்வகிப்பது அடிப்படை கட்டணங்களைத் தாண்டி ஒருங்கிணைப்பு பராமரிப்பு, தரவு சேகரிப்பு, நல்லிணக்க விலகல், ஒப்புதல் கசிவுகள் மற்றும் மாறும் தாமதங்கள் போன்ற மறைக்கப்பட்ட செயல்பாட்டு செலவுகளை உள்ளடக்கியது. வழங்குநர்களைக் குறைப்பதற்குப் பதிலாக, வணிகங்கள் ஒரு ஒருங்கிணைந்த கட்டுப்பாட்டு அடுக்கு, மையப்படுத்தப்பட்ட ரூட்டிங் மற்றும் தானியங்கு அறிக்கையிடல் மூலம் இந்த சவால்களைத் தீர்க்க முடியும்.

This essential infrastructure is needed to price a growing universe of existing assets effectively.

Altius நிறுவனத்தின் இணை நிறுவனர் மற்றும் CEO ஆன Annabelle Huang அவர்களின் கூற்றுப்படி, கிரிப்டோ துறையின் எதிர்காலம் புதிய சொத்துக்களை உருவாக்குவதை விட, வளர்ந்து வரும் ஏற்கனவே உள்ள சொத்துக்களுக்கு விலை நிர்ணயம் செய்யத் தேவையான வலுவான உள்கட்டமைப்பை உருவாக்குவதைச் சார்ந்துள்ளது.

content_ta: ஏழு நாடுகளைச் சேர்ந்த செல்வந்த முதலீட்டாளர்களிடையே நடத்தப்பட்ட சமீபத்திய ஆய்வில், பெரும்பாலானோர் ஏற்கனவே crypto வைத்துள்ளதாகவும், மேலும் முதலீடுகளை அதிகரிக்கத் திட்டமிட்டுள்ளதாகவும் தெரியவந்துள்ளது. டிஜிட்டல் சொத்துக்களில் முதலீடு செய்வது குறித்து நிதி ஆலோசகர்கள் எச்சரிக்கையுடன் இருக்கும் நிலையிலும், செல்வந்தர்களின் இந்த ஆர்வம் அதிகரித்து வருவது குறிப்பிடத்தக்கது.

title: Flash Loan Attacks Drained $1.2B From DeFi Between 2020 and 2024: Study
summary: Attacks grew more sophisticated and less predictable over the period, according to researchers who scanned more than 20 billion transactions.

title: Treasury Drops Crypto Surveillance Proposals
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

This decision is widely viewed as a major victory for the industry, relieving stakeholders from stringent monitoring requirements.
content_ta: கிரிப்டோகரன்சி துறைக்கு ஒரு முக்கிய வெற்றியாக, FinCEN எனப்படும் Financial Crimes Enforcement Network அமைப்பு, அன்ஹோஸ்டெட் வாலட்டுகள் மற்றும் கிரிப்டோகரன்சி மிக்சிங் ஆகியவற்றை இலக்காகக் கொண்ட முன்மொழியப்பட்ட கண்காணிப்பு விதிகளைக் கைவிடுவதாக அறிவித்துள்ளது.

Fedi CEO Obi Nwosu highlighted that this collaborative demonstration addresses critical software-monoculture risks in decentralized custody, showcasing the growing strength and adaptability of the ecash ecosystem.
